News Room

Latest Reports

  • Between September 25-27, 2026, multiple threat actors allegedly conducted widespread credential trafficking operations across dark web marketplaces, offering massive databases containing billions of compromised email-password combinations, stolen payment card data, and personal identifiable information (PII). The scale of these operations is unprecedented, with one actor allegedly claiming access to 35 billion records totaling 1.1TB of data, while another allegedly advertised 15 million credential combinations. Concurrently, specialized fraud marketplaces allegedly emerged offering comprehensive cybercrime-as-a-service platforms, including SIM-swap attacks, social engineering tools, and cryptocurrency draining capabilities. This coordinated marketplace activity represents a significant escalation in the commoditization of stolen data and fraud services, directly threatening organizations across all sectors globally. The immediate risk includes credential stuffing attacks, account takeovers, financial fraud, and unauthorized access to corporate systems. Organizations must urgently implement enhanced authentication controls and credential monitoring to mitigate exposure from these alleged large-scale data compromises.

    • Multiple threat actors allegedly advertised massive credential databases between September 25-27, 2026, including claims of 35 billion email-password combinations (1.1TB) and 15 million URL:LOGIN:PASS records across dark web marketplaces
    • BossShop marketplace allegedly released 34 new stolen payment card databases on September 25, 2026, containing cards from 20 countries with validity rates allegedly ranging from 40-95%, totaling over 7 million cards monthly
    • Specialized fraud-as-a-service marketplaces allegedly emerged offering comprehensive criminal services including SIM-swap attacks, social engineering, database hacking, cryptocurrency drainers, and pig butchering scams with claimed 24-hour response times
    • Educational institutions GlobalAdmissions.com and China-Admissions.com allegedly suffered a data breach with 12.4GB of exfiltrated data appearing on dark web marketplaces on September 26-27, 2026
    • Threat actors allegedly leveraged multiple infrastructure platforms including MediaFire, upload.ee, CloudMarketPro, and dedicated dark web domains to distribute stolen credentials and facilitate fraud operations targeting all industry sectors globally
    Read more

  • Between September 26-27, 2026, multiple significant cybersecurity incidents emerged demonstrating coordinated financial fraud operations, critical infrastructure vulnerabilities, and extensive dark web marketplace activity. Most critically, alleged threat actor Blacknet00 claimed a comprehensive breach of FiveWest, a South African financial services platform, allegedly exfiltrating Firebase authentication keys, cryptocurrency wallet credentials, banking partner data for 25+ South African institutions, and sensitive corporate documentation. Simultaneously, Google allegedly issued warnings about mass exploitation of CVE-2026-35273 in Oracle PeopleSoft by the ShinyHunters group, allegedly targeting education, healthcare, and government sectors globally. Additionally, multiple dark web vendors allegedly advertised extensive inventories of stolen financial credentials, RDP access, and fraud tools across numerous marketplaces. This convergence of events represents a significant escalation in financial cybercrime targeting both enterprise infrastructure and consumer financial data, requiring immediate defensive action across authentication systems, unpatched enterprise software, and financial institution security controls.

    • Alleged threat actor Blacknet00 claimed compromise of FiveWest financial platform, allegedly exfiltrating Firebase/Clerk authentication keys, 16 cryptocurrency wallet private keys, API endpoints, user PII, and corporate documentation including banking credentials for 25+ South African financial institutions
    • Google allegedly warned of mass exploitation of CVE-2026-35273 (CVSS 9.8) in Oracle PeopleSoft by ShinyHunters group, allegedly using WAF bypass techniques and allegedly targeting education, technology, healthcare, agriculture, and government sectors with web shells and trojan deployment
    • Alleged vendor Daksowl allegedly advertised across 7+ dark web markets offering RDP access (US/UK/Japan), SOCKS5 proxies from major ISPs (Comcast, Sprint, AT&T), CVV data, 800+ SSN fullz, and Bank of America/Chase credentials
    • Alleged marketplace operator doc-shop allegedly advertised inventory of 2,647 compromised retail accounts, 7,881 banking credentials, 19,915 fullz records, and credentials for major US banks including Citibank, Chase, Wells Fargo, and American Express
    • Alleged Debay marketplace allegedly advertised comprehensive fraud services including SIM swapping, social media hacking, crypto drainers, casino/pig butchering schemes, and developer recruitment across CryptBB platform
    Read more

  • Multiple threat actors are allegedly operating comprehensive fraud marketplaces on dark web platforms including CryptBB, Dread, and other forums, offering extensive criminal services that pose significant risks to organizations across all sectors. The marketplaces allegedly provide fraud-as-a-service operations including malware distribution (crypto drainers, RATs, keyloggers), social engineering tools, database hacking services, SIM swapping capabilities, and stolen credential databases. This activity represents a concerning trend of commoditized cybercrime where sophisticated attack capabilities are allegedly made accessible to lower-skilled actors. The proliferation of these marketplaces increases the attack surface for organizations globally, particularly those in financial services, technology, and cryptocurrency sectors. The alleged availability of turnkey fraud solutions, combined with escrow systems and reputation mechanisms, creates a sustainable criminal ecosystem that enables persistent threats to organizational security and customer data protection.

    • Multiple threat actors are allegedly advertising comprehensive fraud marketplaces (Debay, ELDRAGON Cyberstore, ZenithBay) on dark web platforms offering criminal services including malware, hacking tools, and social engineering capabilities
    • The alleged marketplaces claim to provide crypto drainers, RATs, keyloggers, SIM swapping services, database hacking, social media account compromise, and email hacking with 24-hour response times
    • Threat actors allegedly offer stolen credential databases organized by geographic region (USA, Europe) via file-sharing platforms like MediaFire, sourced from databases like MonkeyBase
    • The alleged criminal infrastructure includes bulletproof hosting, DDoS services, spamming infrastructure (AWS SES, Mailgun access), and cryptocurrency-based payment systems using Monero (XMR) with escrow protection
    • Alleged services target financial institutions, cryptocurrency platforms, social media networks, and organizations across all sectors with sophisticated attack vectors including pig butchering schemes, casino fraud, and reputation destruction
    Read more

  • Multiple dark web marketplaces, primarily DOC-SHOP and associated platforms, are allegedly conducting large-scale operations selling stolen financial credentials, personally identifiable information (PII), and compromised account access targeting US financial institutions, retail chains, airlines, and payment services. The significance of this activity lies in the comprehensive nature and scale of the alleged data inventory, which reportedly includes over 36,000 complete identity records, 26,000+ fullz packages, 5,600+ bank credentials, and 2,400+ compromised retail accounts. These marketplaces allegedly provide threat actors with ready access to tools and data necessary for identity theft, financial fraud, and account takeover attacks. The timing is critical as these operations appear to be actively maintained with daily updates, suggesting ongoing credential harvesting campaigns. Organizations in the financial services, retail, and travel sectors should prioritize credential monitoring, implement enhanced authentication controls, and educate customers about account security to mitigate the risk of fraud stemming from these alleged compromised datasets.

    • DOC-SHOP marketplace allegedly advertises over 36,200 comprehensive identity records (SSN + DOB + DL + Bank Account + Employer), 26,645 fullz records, and 5,655 bank credentials targeting major US financial institutions including Citibank, Chase, Bank of America, American Express, and Capital One
    • Multiple threat actors (dcshp, Dcshp, cvvFather, WIZARD'S SHOP) are allegedly operating interconnected marketplaces selling stolen credit card data, bank logs, PayPal accounts, SSNs, passports, driver's licenses, and RDP access across clearnet and Tor infrastructure
    • Alleged compromised accounts span major US retailers and service providers including Best Buy, Costco, Verizon, Delta Airlines, Southwest Airlines, Hilton, Ticketmaster, and PayPal, with inventory reportedly exceeding 2,466 shop accounts
    • CryptBB-hosted marketplaces (Debay) allegedly offer fraud-as-a-service including SIM swapping, social engineering, cryptocurrency drainers, database hacking, and email compromise services with 24-hour response times
    • The alleged threat actor motivation is financial gain through credential trafficking, identity theft facilitation, and enabling downstream fraud operations targeting US consumers and financial institutions
    Read more

  • A coordinated surge in dark web marketplace activity has allegedly exposed critical vulnerabilities across financial, government, and enterprise sectors. Multiple threat actors are actively marketing stolen credentials affecting over 38 billion records, compromised payment card data from major retailers and financial institutions, and fraud-as-a-service platforms offering database hacking and social engineering capabilities. Most significantly, a Chinese-speaking threat actor allegedly attributed to Red Heron exploited multiple zero-day and known vulnerabilities (including WordPress Core CVE-2026-63030, CVE-2026-60137, and ZyXEL CVE-2026-7273) to breach government entities across 29 countries, extracting 18,500+ records containing plaintext passwords and PII linked to law enforcement agencies. This represents an escalation in both the scale and sophistication of credential theft operations, with immediate implications for organizations relying on compromised authentication systems and unpatched enterprise infrastructure.

    • Alleged Chinese threat actor Red Heron exploited WordPress Core vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-63030, CVE-2026-60137) and ZyXEL GS1900 switches (CVE-2026-7273) to breach government organizations across 29 countries, extracting 18,566+ records with plaintext credentials and PII from law enforcement databases
    • DOC-SHOP marketplace allegedly offers 42,079 comprehensive identity records (SSN+DL+credit reports), 6,969 banking credentials from major US financial institutions (Bank of America, Chase, Citibank), and compromised data from 2,932 retail websites including Dominos, Hilton, PayPal, and Ticketmaster
    • Multiple threat actors operating Debay fraud marketplace on CryptBB allegedly advertise database hacking, SIM swapping, social media compromise, and crypto drainer services with 24-hour response times and encrypted communication channels
    • Actor Stradu allegedly distributes 1.1TB dataset containing approximately 35 billion records through DB Market platform, with recent additions of 227.5K mail/pass combinations and 2.9 million mixed credential records
    • DarkCC marketplace allegedly promotes quality-controlled stolen credit card and CVV data sales, emphasizing database validation and competitive pricing to attract both buyers and sellers
    Read more

  • Multiple dark web marketplaces are allegedly conducting large-scale operations selling compromised financial data, stolen credentials, and fraud-as-a-service offerings targeting major US financial institutions, retailers, and payment systems. The most significant development is the alleged exposure of over 100,000 compromised financial records including banking credentials from major institutions like Bank of America, Chase, Wells Fargo, and payment card data across multiple marketplaces. These operations represent coordinated criminal infrastructure enabling account takeover attacks, identity theft, and financial fraud at scale. Organizations should immediately review authentication controls, implement enhanced monitoring for credential stuffing attacks, and validate the integrity of customer account access patterns, particularly for financial services and retail sectors.

    • Dark web marketplaces allegedly advertise over 100,000 stolen financial credentials, payment cards, and identity documents targeting major US banks and retailers
    • DOC-SHOP marketplace allegedly offers 9,431 banking credentials from institutions including Bank of America (2,309 entries) and comprehensive identity records with SSN, DOB, and bank account details
    • Multiple fraud-as-a-service platforms allegedly provide SimSwap attacks, social engineering tools, cryptocurrency drainers, and money transfer services across CashApp, PayPal, Zelle, and Apple Pay
    • DarkCC and Hymarket marketplaces allegedly maintain active inventories of stolen credit cards with verification rates up to 75% and authorization success rates up to 75%
    • Threat actors allegedly target financial institutions, major retailers, cryptocurrency exchanges, and email service providers across US, EU, Asia, UK, Canada, and Brazil
    Read more

  • Between September 10-21, 2026, multiple dark web marketplaces allegedly facilitated large-scale trafficking of stolen financial credentials, with threat actors claiming to offer millions of compromised credit cards, bank logs, and personal identifying information across global platforms. Concurrently, a verified North Korean state-sponsored campaign (WaterPlum) allegedly infected approximately 33,000 devices worldwide through job recruitment social engineering between December 2025 and July 2026. This intelligence is significant because it demonstrates the continued industrialization of cybercrime infrastructure, with organized marketplaces providing fraud-as-a-service capabilities targeting financial institutions and individuals globally. The convergence of commodity cybercrime (stolen payment cards) with sophisticated state-sponsored operations (North Korean malware campaigns) indicates an evolving threat landscape requiring coordinated defensive measures across both private sector financial institutions and government cybersecurity agencies.

    • Multiple threat actors allegedly operated verified seller accounts across dark web marketplaces (Debay, WCCM, ToysStash, GIFTCODE, Authorize CC Store) offering stolen credit card data, fullz, bank logs, and cryptocurrency drainer tools between September 10-21, 2026
    • Alleged sales included over 1 million URL-LOG-PASS credentials, thousands of credit cards with claimed validity rates of 52-95%, and targeting victims across 100+ countries including US, UK, Canada, Australia, and throughout Europe and Asia
    • North Korean WaterPlum group allegedly infected 33,000 devices globally (December 2025-July 2026) through job recruitment impersonation, stealing browser passwords, cryptocurrency wallets, and enabling intellectual property theft
    • Threat actors allegedly advertised comprehensive fraud services including SIM swapping, social media hacking, database compromise, crypto drainers, and bot creation with 24-hour response guarantees
    • Financial crime operations allegedly targeted multiple industries with particular focus on finance sector, utilizing Telegram, WhatsApp, and Tor hidden services for communications and transactions
    Read more

  • Between September 20-21, 2026, multiple threat actors allegedly operated coordinated fraud marketplaces on dark web platforms, advertising the sale of tens of thousands of stolen credit card records and comprehensive cybercrime services. The actors claimed to offer over 50,000 compromised payment cards with validity rates between 65-92% at prices ranging from $0.20-$8.00 per card, targeting victims across the United States, Canada, Europe, Asia, and Australia. Simultaneously, verified sellers on CryptBB marketplace allegedly advertised advanced fraud services including cryptocurrency drainer malware, SimSwap attacks, database hacking, and pig butchering schemes. This represents a significant escalation in organized financial cybercrime infrastructure, with threat actors providing turnkey fraud solutions that lower the barrier to entry for cybercriminals. Organizations in the financial sector should immediately review transaction monitoring systems, implement enhanced fraud detection for the affected geographic regions, and prepare incident response procedures for potential compromise of customer payment data.

    • Multiple dark web marketplaces (RobinShop, RavenCVV, ScorpionShop, Debay) allegedly advertised over 50,000 stolen credit card records with claimed validity rates of 65-92% between September 20-21, 2026
    • Threat actors allegedly offered stolen payment card data from victims in the United States, Canada, United Kingdom, Europe, Asia, Australia, and 30+ other countries at prices between $0.20-$8.00 per card
    • Verified sellers on CryptBB marketplace allegedly advertised comprehensive fraud services including cryptocurrency drainer malware, database hacking, SimSwap attacks, social media account compromise, and pig butchering schemes
    • Actors allegedly provided complete personally identifiable information (PII) with stolen cards including names, addresses, ZIP codes, email addresses, phone numbers, and IP addresses to facilitate fraud
    • Multiple threat actors allegedly operated 24/7 customer support services with refund/replacement policies, indicating sophisticated commercial fraud operations with quality assurance mechanisms
    Read more

  • Between September 19-20, 2026, multiple threat actors allegedly operated comprehensive fraud-as-a-service marketplaces across dark web platforms including CryptBB, Dread, and DarkForums. The most significant development is the proliferation of the 'Debay' marketplace, which allegedly offers a full spectrum of cybercriminal services including database hacking, SIM swap attacks, social engineering, cryptocurrency drainers, and pig butchering scams. Concurrently, threat actors allegedly advertised stolen Spanish forex trader databases containing personally identifiable information (PII), and the High-Way market allegedly enhanced its operational security features. This activity represents a maturation of dark web criminal infrastructure, with threat actors allegedly providing turnkey solutions for financial crime, data theft, and unauthorized system access. Organizations across all sectors face elevated risk from these alleged comprehensive attack capabilities, particularly those in finance, technology, and cryptocurrency industries.

    • Multiple threat actors allegedly advertised the 'Debay' fraud marketplace offering database hacking, SIM swap attacks, social media compromise, cryptocurrency drainers, and pig butchering schemes across CryptBB dark web platform
    • Threat actor 'DatabaseMarket' allegedly leaked a database containing PII of 25+ Spanish forex traders including names, email addresses, phone numbers, and IP addresses from 2025-2026
    • The High-Way market operator allegedly detailed enhanced security features including PGP encryption, multisig escrow, FROST threshold signatures, and AppArmor confinement for illicit goods trading
    • Threat actor 'lilsheepyy' allegedly provided guidance on monetizing system access, databases, and Remote Code Execution (RCE) vulnerabilities through dark web sales channels
    • Multiple threat actors allegedly offered cloned credit cards, compromised PayPal accounts, bank logs, and Western Union transfer capabilities via Telegram-based operations
    Read more

  • Multiple threat actors are allegedly operating coordinated financial crime marketplaces across dark web platforms, advertising the sale of stolen payment card data, compromised bank credentials, and cybercrime services. Between September 17-18, 2026, at least 10 distinct actors posted advertisements across five dark web forums (ascarding, cryptbb, altenen, crackingx, xss_is) offering stolen credit cards, bank account access, credential databases totaling over 1.1TB, and hacking services. The actors claim to target major financial institutions including Bank of America, Chase, Wells Fargo, and payment platforms such as PayPal, CashApp, Apple Pay, Venmo, and Zelle. This coordinated activity represents a significant escalation in dark web marketplace operations, with actors allegedly maintaining fresh daily inventory, offering replacement guarantees, and operating across multiple communication channels (Telegram, clearnet, Tor). The convergence of credential aggregation services, financial fraud offerings, and cybercrime-as-a-service platforms indicates a mature criminal ecosystem capable of enabling large-scale financial crime operations targeting mainstream financial services globally.

    • Multiple threat actors allegedly advertised stolen credit card data, bank credentials, and fullz packages across five dark web marketplaces between September 17-18, 2026, targeting major US financial institutions and global payment platforms
    • LeakZero and STRADU_DB allegedly expanded breach databases by 22 million and 270,400 credential pairs respectively, claiming total holdings of approximately 1.1TB of unique data across 35 billion records
    • Debay marketplace allegedly offered comprehensive cybercrime services including database hacking, SIM swapping, social media compromise, cryptocurrency drainers, and reputation destruction across multiple dark web forums
    • Threat actors allegedly claimed 5+ years of experience, daily fresh inventory, 100% live credentials with refund guarantees, and low-risk tested methods for fraud operations
    • Operations allegedly span multiple communication channels including Telegram, clearnet domains, and Tor onion addresses, with actors targeting victims in the US, UK, Canada, EU, and Asia
